chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى الْمَتَوَكِّلُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ الْحِمْيَرِيُّ عَنِ الْأَصْبَغِ بْنِ نُبَاتَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me; he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: خَرَجَ عَلِيٌّ ع ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ وَ نَحْن يَوْمٍ وَ نَحْنُ مُجْتَمِعُونَ فَقَالَ مَنْ أَنْتُمْ وَ مَا اجْتِمَاعُكُمْ فَقُلْنَا قَوْمٌ مِنْ شِيعَتِكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَقَالَ مَا لِي لَا أَرَى سِيمَاءَ الشِّيعَةِ عَلَيْكُمْ فَقُلْنَا وَ مَا سِيمَاءُ الشِّيعَةِ فَقَالَ ع صُفْرُ الْوُجُوهِ مِنْ صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ عُمْشُ الْعُيُونِ مِنْ مَخَافَةِ اللَّهِ ذُبُلُ الشِّفَاهِ مِنَ الصِّيَامِ عَلَيْهِمْ غَبَرَةُ الْخَاشِعِينَ

translations.en: Ali (peace be upon him) went out one day while we were gathered, and he asked: 'Who are you and what is your gathering?' We said: 'A group from your Shia, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'Why do I not see the marks of the Shia upon you?' We asked: 'And what are the marks of the Shia?' He said: 'Pale faces from night prayer, bleary eyes from fear of Allah, dry lips from fasting; upon them is the dust of the humble.'

en.summary: In this renowned hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the 'seal' (simā’) of the Shia not by lineage or title, but by the physical marks of worship: pale faces from night prayer, bleary eyes from fear of God, and dry lips from fasting. This narration establishes a theological framework in Shia tradition where spiritual humility is visibly manifested in the body, linking ascetic practice directly to identity. It serves as a criterion for distinguishing true devotion from nominal affiliation, emphasizing that piety leaves tangible traces on the believer.
en.seo_question: What are the physical signs of true Shia devotion according to Imam Ali?

key_terms.صُفْرُ الْوُجُوهِ: Pale faces (from lack of sleep due to worship)
